observation_summary: The FastDateFormat.format(Date) method produces incorrect week-of-year values because it initializes a GregorianCalendar using only the time zone, ignoring the locale-specific settings (like firstDayOfWeek and minimalDaysInFirstWeek) required for correct date formatting.
hypothesis: The root cause is an incorrect initialization of the GregorianCalendar object within the format(Date) method. By failing to pass the mLocale to the constructor, the calendar defaults to the system's locale settings instead of the locale specified during the FastDateFormat instance creation.
prediction: The fix will involve updating the GregorianCalendar constructor call to include the mLocale field, ensuring the calendar instance respects the intended locale settings.
experiment_rationale: The provided fix diff shows exactly this change: 'new GregorianCalendar(mTimeZone)' was changed to 'new GregorianCalendar(mTimeZone, mLocale)'. This confirms that the issue was an incorrect initialization of the calendar object.
reasoning_summary: The bug is classified as Assignment/Initialization because the fix involves correcting the initialization of a local object (GregorianCalendar). The logic of the formatting algorithm itself is correct, but it was operating on a calendar object initialized with the wrong parameters (missing the locale).

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The procedural logic of formatting is correct; the issue is specifically the initialization of the calendar object used by that procedure.
While it involves passing a parameter, it is an internal object construction within a method, not a contract mismatch between two distinct components.
